packages.label: עָקֵב וְיַעֲקֹב
packages.reason: All three nodes share the essential nature of the humble, lowly dimension that is paradoxically exalted — the 'dal/akev' quality of Yaakov. The text states explicitly: 'יתגדל — תגי דל, שהוא תגי = כתר, דל = בחינת יעקב שהוא עקב בחינת דל.' The heel (עקב) is Jacob's essence — the lowest limb, the heel that trails behind — and that lowliness is the same as 'dal' (the poor one). The Kaddish word 'yitgadal' is parsed as תגי+דל, where 'dalet' specifically represents Jacob-as-heel-as-poor. These three concepts are different expressions of the same essential quality: humble smallness that is Israel's foundational identity and the basis of Kaddish's opening word.

packages.label: מַלְכוּת וְרָצוֹן
packages.reason: All three nodes share the essential nature of divine malkhut as rooted in ratzon (will/desire). The text teaches: 'מלכות הוא בחינת כבוד' (Tehilim 145:11); 'והוא בחינת רצון, כי רצונו של אדם זהו כבודו' (Yerushalmi Peah 1). The Kaddish phrase 'ויַמְלִיךְ מַלְכוּתֵהּ' is conditioned on a person submitting their ratzon entirely to God's ratzon — 'עיקר המלכות מהרצון.' These three concepts are structurally identical: kavod = the outward glory of the king; malkhut = the institution of kingship; ratzon = the inner volitional essence that makes both possible. They are three faces of one domain: the holy kingdom that is constituted and expanded by total submission of will to God.

packages.label: רֹאשׁ וּמֹחִין
packages.reason: These two nodes share the essential nature of the intellectual/spiritual consciousness dimension — the supreme faculty through which a true tzaddik receives holy awareness and can atone for sin. The text states: 'כשנעשה ראש שהוא בחינות מחין, על-ידי-זה הוא יכול לכפר עוונות.' The rosh is not merely a physical head but the spiritual state of 'mochin' — expanded holy consciousness, described also as 'שמן משחת קדש' and 'כשמן הטוב על הראש.' Rosh and mochin are directly equated in the text as the same bechina: being a rosh = having mochin. This is the apex of the Torah's vertical axis — the faculty that enables everything else.
merge_notes: Raw bechina component: {ראש, מחין} — 2 nodes, 1 edge (id=1741: ראש↔מחין). This is a small isolated pair.

Merge candidate considered: Could ראש/מחין merge with מלכות/כבוד/רצון? Rejected — they operate in different domains. Mochin/rosh = the cognitive/spiritual faculty; malkhut/ratzon = the volitional/royal dimension. These are not the same essential nature; they stand in causal relation (mochin → capacity for kavod/ratzon alignment) rather than parallel identity.

Merge candidate considered: Could ראש/מחין merge with עקב/דל/יעקב? Rejected — opposite ends of the vertical axis. עקב/דל = the low/humble; ראש/מחין = the high/expanded. Their relationship is structural (head vs. heel of the same body = the full Kaddish: יתגדל is about the dalet/heel while רבא relates to mochin), not shared nature.
Verdict: Keep as standalone 2-node package. The ראש/מחין pair is a genuine, self-contained conceptual unit central to the Torah's opening argument.
